$comment: This file is what makes the workspace a set of controls rather than a set of documents.
Everything in AGENTS.md was voluntary until these hooks existed.
guard-edit is the only one that BLOCKS (exit 2). It refuses a product-code edit when no
card is in build, when WIP>1, or when the card has no reuse ladder recorded. It ignores
workspace/plan/doc edits deliberately — a guard that fires on everything gets switched
off within a day, and a disabled guard is worse than none because people still trust it.
Override for a genuine emergency: NEXA_NO_CARD=1. It logs rather than passing silently.
Stop hook added after reading Anthropic's large-codebase guidance: it asks the questions whose answers are lost when the window closes — decisions, contract gaps, unmeasured claims.
enabledPlugins names what this workspace depends on rather than what happens to be installed.
codex@openai-codex is load-bearing: it is how a plan gets reviewed by a model that does not
share this one's priors, and it ships a Stop gate that can BLOCK a turn when Codex finds
$plugins: Why each, since §10 says this list names what we DEPEND on rather than what happens to be
installed. Added 2026-07-28 after auditing four proposed plugins and finding that the
marketplace already enabled here carried better matches for this project's actual stack.
code-simplifier      — fills the ponytail gap. §5 calls ponytail part of the contract and
skills/reuse-first is derived from it, but it is not installed and
check.mjs has been failing --strict locally because of it.
security-guidance    — warns at edit time. vibesec runs at deploy and finds 0; this catches
the same class while it is being written. Complement, not replacement:
skills/security-gate is still the thing that cannot be waived.
Add YOUR stack's plugins here — the vendor SDK you actually call, the
host you actually deploy to. Nothing stack-specific ships enabled,
because a plugin declared for somebody else's product is a dependency
nobody on this project asked for.
typescript-lsp       — Anthropic's large-codebase guidance, practice 4: LSP returns the
references that point to the SAME symbol, so filtering happens before
Claude reads anything. It serves JavaScript, which is all this repo is.
Complements graphify rather than replacing it: the graph answers
"what relates to what", the LSP answers "exactly which callers".
Declined the same day, with reasons in docs/DECISIONS.md: claude-mem and claude-obsidian.
Both put the record somewhere a diff cannot reach it, which is the same test that declined
Hindsight an hour earlier. Consistency here is the point — the rule is not about any one
tool, it is that memory this project relies on has to be reviewable.
